documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

62 y/o woman transferring care; her longtime PCP is retiring. Retired from retail (store supervisor, 20+ yrs on her feet). Here alone.

Problems she brings:
- HTN x ~9 yrs, on HCTZ 25 daily. Checks BP at the pharmacy machine now and then, "usually in the 120s."
- T2DM dx ~2011, metformin 1000 BID. Last A1c she remembers was "around 7." No hypoglycemia (not on anything that would cause it). Mild GI upset when she started metformin, long gone.
- Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 40 since the diabetes dx. No myalgias.
- Weight: has been heavy since her 40s. Tried a commercial program twice.
- Smoker: 1 ppd since about age 30, so ~32 pack-years. Has cut down before but never quit for more than a few weeks. Not interested in a plan today.

PSH: hysterectomy at 48, lap chole at 52. No complications.
FHx: mother has late-onset Alzheimer's (dx at 78). Father had T2DM, HTN, high cholesterol, died of an MI at 72. Maternal grandmother had glaucoma. Sister has osteoarthritis.
SHx: divorced, one grown daughter nearby. No alcohol. No drugs.
Meds: HCTZ 25 qAM, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40 qHS.
Allergies: NKDA

ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, claudication, polyuria, numbness in feet, vision change, GI or GU complaints.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI 33. Pleasant, NAD. Fundi not well seen undilated. Neck supple, no thyromegaly, no bruits. RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abd obese, soft, well-healed lap scars. No edema. Feet: skin intact, no calluses, pulses 2+ DP/PT, monofilament intact bilaterally.

A/P
1. HTN - at goal on HCTZ. CMP today.
2. T2DM - A1c, UACR, lipids drawn this morning. Continue metformin. Wants an eye exam this year with her usual optometrist.
3. HLD - continue atorvastatin 40.
4. Obesity BMI 33 - talked about walking; she's open to it.
5. Tobacco use - advised to quit, gave quitline number. Lung screening to discuss next visit when she's had time to think.
6. HM - HCV and HIV screening once (agreed). Mammogram ordered. Records request for colonoscopy date. Flu shot next month when we get stock.
RTC 6 months, sooner prn.

See you in March, and please do the mammogram when you can.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OPHTHALMOLOGY CONSULTATION -- date of service 06/10/2021
Referred by primary care for vision loss.

History: Over roughly six months both eyes have slowly lost clarity. Painless. She has had no redness or discharge. Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia. Smoker, 35 pack-years. Maternal grandmother had glaucoma.
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Examination:
Visual acuity reduced in each eye.
Intraocular pressure (Goldmann): 28 mmHg OD, 27 mmHg OS.
Gonioscopy: angles open 360 degrees both eyes. Anterior chambers deep and quiet.
Optic nerves: enlarged cup-to-disc ratio both eyes.
Humphrey visual fields: central fields preserved; peripheral field loss in both eyes.
Dilated fundus: no diabetic retinopathy; macula flat.

Impression: Primary open-angle glaucoma, both eyes.
Plan: Start latanoprost 0.005%, one drop in each eye at bedtime. Reviewed drop technique and the possibility of iris darkening and lash growth. Recheck pressure in 8 weeks. Fields and OCT yearly. Okay to drive in daylight.
Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Rheumatology Consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY NEW CONSULT -- visit 11/29/2021
Reason: hand pain, referred by PCP.

Ms. Klein, 65, reports a year of progressively worse pain in both hands. It is at its worst on waking and eases as she uses her hands during the day. No joint redness or warmth. Background: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, recently diagnosed open-angle glaucoma.
Meds: HCTZ 25 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, atorvastatin 40 mg, latanoprost drops. NKDA.
Social: current smoker, 35 pack-years; no alcohol; retired retail supervisor.
Family: sister with osteoarthritis.

Exam: Bony hypertrophy of the DIP and PIP joints bilaterally with mild tenderness to palpation. Crepitus on passive range of motion. No erythema, warmth or soft-tissue swelling. MCPs and wrists spared.
Hand radiographs (today): joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis and periarticular osteophytes at the involved joints, no erosive change.

Assessment: Primary osteoarthritis of the hands. No features of an inflammatory arthritis.
Plan: Acetaminophen scheduled or as needed; hand therapy exercises (handout given); paraffin/warm soaks in the morning. Return as needed or if other joints become involved.

documents.title: Rheumatology
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Did you get the letter from the arthritis doctor? She said it's just wear and tear, take Tylenol. Is that it? I thought maybe there was a pill.

documents.title: RE: Rheumatology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Got it, thanks. I agree with her -- osteoarthritis in the finger joints, not the inflammatory kind. Acetaminophen plus the hand exercises and warm water in the mornings is the right start. Anti-inflammatories carry more risk for your kidneys and blood pressure, so I'd hold off. We'll keep an eye on it.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Right knee has been getting steadily worse for about six months. Hurts with walking and stairs, eases when she sits. Getting out of a chair after a long sit is the hard part. Both knees stiff in the morning but loosen within 20 minutes. No swelling, no locking, no injury.

X-rays both knees today (in-office): joint space narrowing and osteophytes bilaterally.
A/P:
1. Osteoarthritis, both knees (R symptomatic). She asked what she can do to cut the long-term toll rather than just patching pain. Discussed: weight loss is the biggest lever (each pound off is several off the knee), quadriceps strengthening, low-impact activity. PT referral placed for a home program. Continue acetaminophen as needed; topical options if needed later.
2. T2DM -- A1c today (due).
3. Tobacco -- also slows healing of everything; counseled.

Recurrent severe right knee pain; activity tolerance down. Worse with use, better with rest. No fall or injury.

documents.title: Sick Visit: Rash
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Two days of burning on the right side of her chest wrapping toward the back, then blisters came up this morning. No fever. No eye symptoms. Never had the shingles shot.
O: Afebrile. Grouped vesicles on an erythematous base in a band along the right T5 dermatome, front to back, not crossing midline. No lesions on face/nose. Rest of skin clear.
A/P: Herpes zoster, right T5, within 72 h. Valacyclovir 1 g TID x 7 days. Acetaminophen for pain; cool compresses. Keep lesions covered around anyone pregnant or immunocompromised. Call if spreading, eye involvement, or pain uncontrolled. Shingrix after this settles -- she says now she'll take it.

documents.title: Shingles
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Blisters are crusting over. Still burns. Finished 5 days of the pills, 2 to go. Is it okay to go to my sister's cookout?

documents.title: RE: Shingles
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Once every blister has crusted over you're no longer contagious, so yes if they're all crusted. Finish the full 7 days. Let us know if the pain isn't easing.

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROLOGY CONSULTATION -- 12/05/2023
Referral: persistent pain after shingles.

67-year-old woman with glaucoma and osteoarthritis. About five months ago she had shingles on the right chest, treated with valacyclovir; the pain never went away. It is sharp and shooting, and even light touch sets it off. Over-the-counter acetaminophen and ibuprofen have not helped.
Other history: hypertension (HCTZ), type 2 diabetes (metformin), hyperlipidemia. Smoker, 35 pack-years. NKDA.

Exam: hyperpigmentation and scarring in the right T5 dermatome. A cotton swab drawn lightly across the area produces severe pain (allodynia). Strength, reflexes and sensation otherwise normal. No active lesions.

Assessment: Postherpetic neuralgia, right T5. Acute zoster resolved.
Plan: Gabapentin 300 mg at bedtime, increasing every 5 days to 300 mg three times daily. Counseled on dizziness and sleepiness; take care on stairs, no driving if drowsy. Follow up in 3 months, or PCP can continue if stable.

Neurology said we can manage refills here if stable -- happy to.
Meds: HCTZ 25, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40, latanoprost OU qHS, gabapentin 300 TID, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.
O: BP fine. Right T5 band still tender to touch, healed skin. Gait steady.
A/P:
1. PHN -- improving on gabapentin. Continue; refills from us. Kidney function normal so dose is fine.
2. T2DM -- A1c today.
3. Shingrix: now's a good time; first dose at a nurse visit, second 2-6 mo later.

RHEUMATOLOGY FOLLOW-UP -- 06/10/2024
Ms. Klein returns with progressive osteoarthritis. We saw her for her hands in 2021, and orthopedics saw her right knee in 2022 and 2023. Knees ache and stiffen after standing or walking for a while; rest helps, the day makes it worse. She has noticed bony swellings developing on her fingers.
Meds: HCTZ 25, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40, latanoprost, gabapentin 300 TID (for post-shingles pain), acetaminophen. NKDA. Smoker, 35 pack-years.

Exam: right knee tender along the medial joint line; Heberden nodes at the DIP joints; no warmth, erythema or swelling of any joint. Right side worse than left.
Procedure: a small-volume aspirate was obtained from the right knee under sterile technique to exclude an inflammatory or crystal process. Synovial fluid: white cell count 420 cells/uL, no crystals -- noninflammatory.

Assessment: Generalized (nodal) osteoarthritis -- hands and knees, R knee most symptomatic. No inflammatory arthritis.
Plan: continue acetaminophen, strengthening and weight management. Return as needed.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit and Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV + chronic care visit. 69F, here with her daughter.

Daughter's concerns (pt present, agrees "a little"): over roughly the last 10 months mom has been more forgetful -- misplacing her keys and glasses, repeating questions on the phone, mixed up the January appointment week. Still managing her own pills with the alarm box; daughter checks the box on Sundays now. Pt feels it's normal aging; her own mother had Alzheimer's late in life and she's worried about that.
No falls, no head injury, no new meds since gabapentin in late 2023. Mood fine -- PHQ-2 0. No alcohol.

Chronic problems: HTN, T2DM, HLD, obesity, tobacco use (1 ppd, ~39 pack-years), POAG (ophtho, stable), nodal OA hands/knees, PHN on gabapentin.
Meds: HCTZ 25, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40, latanoprost OU qHS, gabapentin 300 TID, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, pleasant, conversant, a bit hesitant on dates. Neuro: no focal deficits, gait normal. Heart/lungs normal. Feet normal.

A/P:
1. Memory concerns, ~10 months, family history. Reversible causes: TSH and B12 with today's labs. Gabapentin can dull thinking -- she's on a modest dose and it's controlling the pain, so leave for now. Referral to geriatric psychiatry memory clinic for a full evaluation (wait is long, ~6 months). Daughter to help with appointments and medications.
2. T2DM / HTN / HLD -- labs today; no changes.
3. Tobacco -- counseled again. LDCT due -- ordered.
4. PHN -- stable on gabapentin, refills here.
F/u 6 months, or after the memory evaluation.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Dorothy (and Karen-on-copy if Dorothy shares this): labs from Tuesday are good. Thyroid normal, B12 normal -- so nothing simple there to explain the memory changes, which is why the memory clinic visit matters. A1c a little above 7, fine for you with no change. Kidneys fine, cholesterol at goal. The memory clinic will call to schedule; let us know if you don't hear in 3 weeks.

documents.title: Geriatric Psychiatry Consultation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
GERIATRIC PSYCHIATRY -- MEMORY CLINIC CONSULTATION, 12/01/2025
Referred by PCP for memory evaluation.

Ms. Klein is a 69-year-old woman accompanied by her daughter, who reports a year and a half of steadily worsening forgetfulness and confusion. She misplaces everyday items around the house, has lost her way driving on roads she knows well, and at times cannot find the word she wants. Her daughter also notes she is more irritable than she used to be, with some change in personality.
History: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, open-angle glaucoma, osteoarthritis, postherpetic neuralgia. Current smoker, 35 pack-years; no alcohol. Mother with late-onset Alzheimer disease.
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, atorvastatin 40 mg, latanoprost OU, gabapentin 300 mg TID, acetaminophen. NKDA.

Exam: oriented to person only -- not to place or date. Neurologic exam without focal findings. MMSE 22/30.
MRI brain (11/20/2025): diffuse cortical atrophy, greatest in the hippocampi and temporal lobes.
Prior labs from PCP (TSH, B12) normal.

Impression: Alzheimer disease.
Plan:
- Donepezil 5 mg at bedtime; increase to 10 mg after 4 weeks if tolerated. Possible nausea, vivid dreams, slow pulse.
- Daughter to supervise medications.
- Follow up 6 weeks.
cc: PCP
